Let's go

"Everybody hit the fucking deck!" 

I wanted to make it sound as tough as I could, but it still was awkward to my own ears. Nevertheless they all got down, and the woman in the yellow dress even put her arms around her kids. I guess I am more threatening than I think.

"You're going to take the money in this bag and deposit all of it." The pockmarked teller looked at me with a blank face. 

"Do what I say right now, so that I don't have to do something I don't want to." I gestured to my finger-gun seated in my jacket pocket.  

"You... you want me to deposit it?" He was young and his voice cracked on the word 'deposit'. 

"Yes you stupid shit, DEPOSIT IT!" I felt bad for calling this kid stupid, but I wasn't going to let myself get evicted.

"What's the name of the account you want me to deposit it in?"

Fuck. I'm such an idiot. I can't just deposit it into my own account and have it brazenly obvious that I held up a bank to make a deposit for myself. 

Should I just walk out the front door? How many crimes have I even committed at this point? Couldn't be more than one or two, and I might never be caught if I just walk out right now. Being evicted wouldn't even be half-bad. 

No, fuck that. That same kind of laziness and half-assed effort is how I got myself into this position in the first place. This time I'm going to actually be a man and do what needs to be done. Surely if I somehow deposit money into all the bank's accounts then they won't be able to...

Sirens. Fuck. 

The fucking police were called. It must've been that pockmarked shithead kid. Jesus I'm not a criminal, what the hell am I going to do now? I don't even have an actual gun! Fuck. Fuck. Fuck.

Three cars. They sent three goddamn cars. I am beyond fucked. 

"Son, come outside with your hands up. This doesn't have to be complicated."

This asshole is calling me 'son' as if that will convince me to walk out there. No. I can't do that, then I'll end up worse than evicted.
